topic.name: Metformin
topic.short_description: Diabetes medication showing promise in cancer prevention and treatment
topic.seo_title: Metformin in Cancer Research - Latest Studies & Findings | Your Cancer Breakthroughs
topic.seo_description: Explore metformin's potential in cancer prevention and treatment. Discover latest peer-reviewed research on this diabetes medication's off-label cancer applications.
topic.seo_intro:
Metformin is a commonly prescribed medication for type 2 diabetes that has gained significant attention in cancer research circles. Originally developed to manage blood sugar levels, researchers have begun investigating whether this affordable, well-tolerated drug might offer additional benefits in cancer prevention and treatment. The medication's mechanism of action—which includes reducing insulin levels, activating cellular energy sensors, and potentially inhibiting cancer cell growth—has sparked considerable scientific interest in recent years.

The connection between metformin and cancer emerged from epidemiological observations showing that diabetic patients taking metformin had lower cancer incidence rates compared to those on other diabetes medications. This observation prompted numerous laboratory and clinical investigations to understand whether metformin could slow cancer development or enhance the effectiveness of standard cancer treatments. While metformin is not an approved cancer medication, its potential as an off-label therapeutic option is being actively explored in multiple cancer types, including breast, colorectal, pancreatic, and lung cancers.

On this page, you'll find comprehensive information about metformin's role in cancer research, including how it may work against cancer cells, the current state of clinical and preclinical studies, and what experts say about its potential benefits and limitations. The articles and resources below represent the latest peer-reviewed research and medical insights on this promising therapeutic avenue. Whether you're a patient, caregiver, or simply seeking to understand emerging cancer treatments, this information is intended to inform your conversations with your healthcare team.

articles.title: Alogliptin-metformin synergy ameliorates diabetes-associated bone loss via modulation of DPP-4 activity and OPG/RANKL signaling.
articles.hook: Alogliptin-metformin combination restores bone density in diabetic models
articles.summary: Combined alogliptin-metformin treatment protects bones in diabetic rats by reducing inflammation and restoring bone-regulating protein balance.

articles.title: Reductive death is averted by a conserved de novo lipogenic switch.
articles.hook: Metformin requires de novo lipogenesis to prevent reductive stress in cancer cells
articles.summary: Metformin's life-extending benefits require intact fat-making pathways to prevent toxic chemical buildup; this vulnerability could target certain cancers.

articles.title: M.globosa promotes lung cancer progression and M2 macrophage polarization through oxidative phosphorylation.
articles.hook: Metformin blocks M.globosa-driven lung cancer progression via macrophage metabolism
articles.summary: M.globosa fungus promotes lung cancer growth by activating immune cells through a metabolic process that can be blocked by metformin.

articles.title: Metformin sensitizes esophageal squamous cell carcinoma to Vγ9Vδ2 T cell-mediated cytotoxicity by upregulating BTN3A1 and BTN2A1.
articles.hook: Metformin enhances immune T cell killing of esophageal cancer via BTN3A1 upregulation
articles.summary: Metformin enhances esophageal cancer cell death by increasing proteins that activate immune T cells to attack tumors.

articles.title: A Self-Cascade Nanozyme of Metformin-Stabilized Amorphous Iron Oxide With Ultrahigh Fe(II) for Potent Tumor Therapy at Ultralow Dose.
articles.hook: Metformin-stabilized iron oxide nanozymes kill cancer cells at ultralow doses in hypoxic tumors
articles.summary: Low-dose iron oxide nanoparticles generate hydrogen peroxide to trigger cancer cell death effectively, even in oxygen-poor tumors.

articles.title: Single-nucleus interrogation of primate small intestinal aging reveals NCoR1 decline as a conserved feature that is reversed by metformin.
articles.hook: Metformin restores NCoR1 levels in aged primate intestinal cells
articles.summary: Metformin reverses age-related intestinal decline by restoring NCoR1 protein levels in primates and human cells.

articles.title: Non-enzymatic RNA Glycation is a Metabolic Sensor of Cellular Stress
articles.hook: Metformin reverses RNA glycation-induced protein synthesis impairment in pancreatic cells
articles.summary: RNA glycation from metabolic stress impairs protein production and insulin secretion in pancreatic cells, but metformin reverses this effect.

articles.title: Exploration of BMI and circulating metabolic factors as predictors of metformin benefit in CCTG MA.32.
articles.hook: Obesity markers predict metformin benefit in HER2-positive breast cancer
articles.summary: Metformin showed potential benefit in HER2-positive breast cancer patients, with obesity-related blood markers possibly predicting treatment response.

articles.title: Combined purslane ethanolic extract and metformin attenuate cognitive dysfunction in HFD/STZ-induced diabetic rats via modulation of oxidative stress, neuroinflammation, and neurotransmitters.

articles.summary: Purslane extract combined with metformin improved memory problems in diabetic rats by reducing brain inflammation and oxidative stress.

articles.title: Metformin counteracts lipid accumulation and cell proliferation in hepatocellular carcinoma via regulating METTL3-mediated m6A methylation.
articles.hook: Metformin reduces lipid accumulation and proliferation in hepatocellular carcinoma via METTL3 inhibition
articles.summary: Metformin reduces lipid buildup and cancer cell growth in liver cancer by decreasing a protein that modifies RNA structure.
